title: Reliable delivery: sequence, ack, resume, replay, dedupe
goal: Guarantee ordered, at-least-once, de-duplicated delivery of sequenced frames over any transport: track `seq`, send acks on the contract cadence, resend unacked outbound frames with the same ids after reconnect, and handle resume results.
scope_in: `ReliableChannel` wrapping a `FrameLink` (the RelayClient shape: send, frame events, welcome, link state) so it works unchanged over relay and LAN.

Outbound: client-generated monotonic ULID `msg_` ids, an unacked map keyed by id, echo-as-ack (the server echoes our sequenced frame with its `seq`), resend in original order after every `welcome`, periodic resend of frames unechoed for > 30 s (max 3 times, then `stuck` event).

Inbound: strictly in-order delivery by `seq` with `lastSeq` (highest contiguous processed), drop of duplicates (`seq <= lastSeq`), a bounded out-of-order hold buffer (1 000 frames, 5 s) and gap recovery by sending `sys.resume {last_seq}` then reconnecting if the gap persists.
Ack cadence: piggy-back `ack = lastSeq` on every outbound frame; standalone `{t:'ack', ack:n}` at least every 5 s while there are unacked inbound frames and after every 64 frames processed.

Resume handling: supply `last_seq` for hello; process `sys.resumed {from_seq,to_seq,count}` (verify contiguity and count) and `sys.resumed {snapshot_required:true, snapshot_seq}` (emit `snapshot-required`, wait for `resumeFrom(seq)`); `applyHistory(frames)` to feed REST history frames through the same dedupe path.
Optional `SeqStore` persistence hook so `lastSeq` survives a process restart (default in-memory).
scope_out: Socket, handshake, heartbeat, backoff: lane C054.
Decrypting or verifying frames; interpreting kinds: lanes C056, C057 and the feature lanes.
Downloading and decrypting snapshots, REST history paging: lane C057.
Disk persistence of the outbound queue across restarts and offline UX: lane C063.
Host-side sequencing for LAN (assigning `seq`): lane C072.
build_against: the mock backend (lane C007): REST from OpenAPI plus the WebSocket relay simulator, started in-process with `startMockBackend()` from @centcom/testkit; no real backend is needed. The relay simulator assigns seq, echoes, replays from a configurable hot buffer, and can drop, duplicate or reorder deliveries and answer `snapshot_required` (`relay.dropNext(3)`, `relay.duplicate(seq)`, `relay.setHotBuffer(10)`). Frames and edge cases come from contracts/fixtures/envelope/.
interfaces: `new ReliableChannel(opts: { link: FrameLink; sessionId: string; memberId?: () => string | null; seqStore?: SeqStore; clock; ids: IdGenerator; logger; maxUnacked?: number /*1000*/; maxUnackedBytes?: number /*8 MiB*/ })`

`send(draft: { t: 'event'|'queue'|'control'; k: string; p?: object; ct?: Ciphertext; sig?: string; ref?: string; id?: string }): Promise<{ id: string; seq: number }>` resolves when the echo with `seq` arrives; rejects `OutboxFullError` at the caps
`sendEphemeral(draft: { t: 'presence'; k: string; p?: object; ct?: Ciphertext; sig?: string }): void` (no id, no resend, no buffering)
Events: `frame(f: SequencedFrame)` (in order, exactly once per seq), `snapshot-required({snapshotSeq})`, `resumed({fromSeq,toSeq,count})`, `stuck({id})`, `gap({expected,got})`

Methods: `lastSeq(): number | null`, `pending(): number`, `resumeFrom(seq: number): Promise<void>` (sets lastSeq then sends `sys.resume {last_seq}`), `applyHistory(frames: SequencedFrame[]): number` (returns applied count), `drain(timeoutMs): Promise<void>`
`interface SeqStore { load(sid: string): Promise<number | null>; save(sid: string, seq: number): Promise<void> }`
`FrameLink` (type imported from lane C054's `relay/index.ts`): `{ send(f): Promise<void>; on(ev: 'welcome'|'frame'|'link'|'closed', fn): () => void; welcome: Welcome | null; state: string }`
`FrameLink` (type imported from lane C054's `relay/index.ts`): `{ send(f): Promise<void>; on(ev: 'welcome'|'frame'|'link'|'closed', fn): () => void; welcome: Welcome | null; state: string }`
acceptance: After a forced close with 4 unacked frames, the client reconnects within 15 s, resends exactly those 4 frames in original order with the same ids, and the mock records zero duplicate (sid, from, id) deliveries; each `send()` promise resolves with the seq from the echo.
With the mock delivering seq 5,5,6,7,7 after seq 4, `frame` fires exactly for 5,6,7 once each and `lastSeq()` ends at 7.
With the mock delivering 1,2,4,3 the channel emits 1,2,3,4 in order (hold buffer), never 4 before 3.

A permanent gap (3 never arrives) triggers `sys.resume {last_seq: 2}` after 5 s and a forced reconnect if still missing after a further 5 s; hold buffer never exceeds 1 000 frames (1 001st gap-frame triggers reconnect).

Ack timing on a fake clock: 100 inbound frames in 1 s produce acks after frames 64 and (at the latest) 5 s later for the remainder; with no inbound frames no standalone ack is sent; every outbound frame carries `ack == lastSeq`.
Resume inside the hot buffer: hello carries `last_seq`, replayed frames last_seq+1..head arrive, `sys.resumed {from_seq,to_seq,count}` is checked (a count mismatch emits `gap` and reconnects).

`sys.resumed {snapshot_required:true, snapshot_seq:900}` emits `snapshot-required` with 900 and holds delivery; after `resumeFrom(900)` the next frames start at seq 901 and `lastSeq()` becomes contiguous from 900.
`applyHistory()` of REST frames 901..950 followed by WS replay 940..960 delivers 901..960 exactly once each.
Ids are strictly increasing within 10 000 sends in one millisecond window (monotonic ULID) and match `^msg_[0-9A-HJKMNP-TV-Z]{26}$`.
Property test (1 000 random schedules of drop/duplicate/reorder/disconnect): the delivered sequence is always the gap-free prefix 1..N in order, and no sent id is delivered twice by the mock.
`send()` rejects with OutboxFullError when 1 000 frames or 8 MiB are unacked; ephemeral presence frames are never retained or resent.
tests: delivery/inbox.test.ts: duplicate, reorder, gap, hold-buffer limits.
delivery/outbox.test.ts: resend order, echo matching by id, stuck handling, caps.
delivery/ack-scheduler.test.ts: 5 s timer and 64-frame threshold on a fake clock.
delivery/resume.test.ts: hot-buffer resume, snapshot_required, history overlap, count mismatch.
delivery/property.test.ts: fast-check schedules with a deterministic seed, asserts ordering and exactly-once.
delivery/conformance.test.ts: replays contracts/fixtures/envelope/ scenarios against the channel.
guardrails: MUST resend unacked frames with the SAME `id` (never regenerate) so the (sid, from, id) de-dup holds; MUST NOT resend before `welcome` is received.
MUST deliver to subscribers strictly in `seq` order and exactly once; MUST NOT deliver a frame past a gap.
MUST NOT treat presence, ping, pong or notice frames as sequenced; they are never buffered, acked or replayed.
`lastSeq` MUST advance on in-order receipt even when the layer above cannot decode a frame (it is dropped, not retried); otherwise one undecodable frame would stall the whole session.
MUST NOT hold unbounded memory: outbox 1 000 frames / 8 MiB, hold buffer 1 000 frames, dedupe id cache 5 000 entries.
MUST NOT log frame bodies; log seq numbers, counts and ids only.
failure_modes: Echo never arrives (server dropped the frame) -> resend at 30 s, up to 3 times, then emit `stuck` and keep the frame in the outbox for the next reconnect rather than discarding user work.
Server replays from a point before our `lastSeq` -> duplicates ignored silently.
Server's `seq` jumps backwards (relay reset) -> emit `gap` with a protocol warning, force reconnect with `last_seq:null`, rely on snapshot/history.
SeqStore load fails -> start with `last_seq:null` (full resume path), log a warning.
notes: CONTRACT GAP: the pure ack frame is described as `{ack: n}`; this card sends `{v:1,t:'ack',sid,ack:n}` using the top-level `ack` field of the envelope.
